title: Map Telegram sign-in state to user-visible diagnostic classes

findings.trace: Ctrl-C raises UsageError('interactive sign-in cancelled'); enroll catch calls telegramFailure; non-TelegramConnectorError becomes ConnectionError('Telegram sign-in did not complete; existing source state was preserved.'); dispatch prints error: … and returns 1.
findings.affected_invariant: Cancel should be a distinct usage/cancel class (exit 2), as the preamble promises Ctrl-C and IMAP preserves UsageError.

findings.trace: flood_wait is special-cased only when retry_after is a safe integer > 0; otherwise notices[flood_wait] is undefined and the connectivity fallback is used.
findings.affected_invariant: Unavailable-wait must keep a wait diagnosis, not invent a connectivity cause.
findings.required_fix: P048: map flood_wait without seconds to a wait/unavailable sentence, not connectivity.

findings.trace: Blank-abandon, third refused credential, and unoccupied-number refuseRegistration all throw sign_in_aborted; CLI uses one cancel sentence.
findings.affected_invariant: Cancel vs unavailable (no account) are distinct owner actions.
findings.required_fix: P048 may keep current copy as characterization or split classes; do not silently treat no-account as owner cancel.

findings.trace: ConnectionError('Telegram state is missing') is thrown inside try and rewritten by telegramFailure to generic incomplete.
findings.affected_invariant: Host selection/state errors thrown outside try stay specific; the same class inside try does not.

findings.trace: closed, missing_session, parse_error, unreachable all become 'Telegram sign-in failed. Check connectivity…'.
findings.affected_invariant: Unavailable should not claim connectivity when the session is merely missing.
